title: Radio (Vivid VH-109)
summary: Power, PoE vs barrel, link lights, programming, DS Wi-Fi in the pit.

start.question: Look at the five lights on the radio. What do you see?
start.help: Left to right: PWR, SYS, 2.4G, 6G, RIO.

options.label: PWR off
PWR on, SYS off
PWR on, SYS blinking once a second
PWR on, SYS blinking very fast
All lights blinking fast
SYS solid, RIO light off
Lights look fine but robot has no comms

dc-only.title: No power on the DC input
steps: Tug the Weidmuller plug at the radio. Pull the wires, strip fresh copper, push them back in until they lock.
Check polarity. Red to plus, black to minus. Reversed polarity does not light the radio.
Check the PDH or PDP channel that feeds the radio. Reseat the fuse or breaker. A red channel LED means no output.
Measure at the plug. The radio takes battery voltage up to 19 V. No voltage means the wiring, not the radio.

steps.text: Is the radio still dark with 12 V at the plug?
steps.yes: Swap the radio and program it at the kiosk.

poe-only.title: No power over PoE
steps: PoE comes in on the RIO port only. Move the cable if it is in AUX1, AUX2, or DS.

Check the injector orientation. On the orange REV injector the male end plugs into the radio. On the black Vivid injector the female end takes the PoE, with a cable from there to the radio's RIO port.
Check the injector or PoE cable is powered from a PDH or PDP channel with a good fuse.
Swap the Ethernet cable between injector and radio. A cable with a broken pair carries data but not power.
Use the DC plug instead and take the PoE power off if the team has it wired.

steps.text: Is the radio still dark?
steps.yes: Swap the radio and program it at the kiosk.

dual-power.title: PoE and DC input at the same time
steps: Two power inputs from different sources or voltages make the radio reboot or drop. This is a known bad setup.
Pick one. Remove the power from the PoE injector and keep the Ethernet for data, or remove the DC plug.
Vivid allows dual feed only from the same source at the same voltage. Most teams do not have that. Use one.
Power cycle the radio after the change and wait 60 seconds for SYS.

steps.text: Does the radio still reboot or stay dark?
steps.yes: Follow the DC only or PoE only branch.

rpm.title: Radio Power Module
steps: Do not power the radio from the RPM and the 12 V DC input at the same time. It can damage the radio.
Check the RPM input has 12 V from its PDH or PDP channel and its own LED is on.
Check the RPM output cable goes to the radio RIO port.
Wire the radio straight to a PDH or PDP channel if the RPM is suspect. Vivid recommends fewer devices between the battery and the radio.

steps.text: Is the radio still dark?
steps.yes: Swap the radio and program it at the kiosk.

booting.title: PWR on, SYS off: still booting
steps: Wait 60 seconds. SYS stays off during boot.
Power cycle the radio once if SYS never comes on after 2 minutes.
A radio that loops power and never finishes boot may have the old flash corruption bug. Fixed in 1.2.5. Take it to the kiosk to update.
Check the supply voltage is steady. A weak battery or loose plug can hold the radio in boot.

steps.text: Is SYS still off?

where.question: Where is the robot right now?
where.help: SYS blinking once a second means the radio cannot ping the field access point.

options.label: On the field
In the pit or practice area

field-not-linked.title: On the field, radio cannot reach the AP
steps: Wait 60 seconds after power on.
Reprogram the radio at this event's kiosk if it came from home or another event.
Check for a second radio programmed for this event left powered on, often a spare at the pit. It associates with the field and confuses the connection.
The radio links to the field AP on its own and its status lights show that. The field monitor shows a partial connection until the DS is fully connected, then it goes green.
Check the radio is mounted in the open, not inside a metal frame or printed box. Move it if needed.

steps.text: Is SYS still blinking once a second?

pit-not-linked.title: In the pit, SYS blinking is normal
steps: In the pit there is no field AP, so SYS blinks. That is expected.
A team's own practice AP must be set as an access point with the same key. That is not allowed on the event floor.
Do not reprogram the radio to home settings. It must stay on this event's kiosk settings.
Connect the DS with an Ethernet cable into the radio DS port for pit testing.

flashing.title: SYS blinking very fast: firmware update
steps: 20 Hz blink means firmware is writing. 50 Hz means the first boot after an update.
Do not power off. Wait until SYS goes solid or slow blink. This can take 2 minutes.
Power cycle once if it has been more than 5 minutes. Take it to the kiosk to check the firmware version.

steps.text: Is SYS still blinking very fast?

ap-battery.title: All lights blinking: AP mode on battery
steps: The radio is configured as an Access Point and sees battery power. Wireless is off.
Take it to the kiosk and program it in Robot Radio mode for this event.
Check the team did not put a practice AP radio on the robot by mistake.

steps.text: Do all lights still blink after a reprogram?

rio-link.title: RIO light off: no link to the roboRIO
steps: Confirm the roboRIO is powered and booted. Its Status light goes off when boot completes.
Reseat the Ethernet cable at both ends.
Try a known good cable.
Power cycle the radio.

steps.text: Is there still no link?

steps: Connect the roboRIO to a laptop by Ethernet directly, bypassing the radio.

steps.text: Does the laptop connect to the roboRIO?

steps: Plug a USB Ethernet dongle into the roboRIO USB port and connect the laptop through it.

steps.text: Does the dongle connect?
steps.yes: Check the roboRIO web UI for a bad NIC config.
steps.no: The roboRIO Ethernet is dead. Swap the roboRIO.

programmed.question: Was this radio programmed at this event's kiosk?

options.label: No, or not sure
Yes, today

reprogram.title: Program the radio at the kiosk
steps: Take the radio, or the robot, to the radio kiosk. Enter the team number. The kiosk sets the event key and updates firmware if needed.
Do not use the radio's own web page at an event. Only the kiosk has the right key.
Power the radio from the robot after programming and wait 60 seconds. SYS goes solid on the field.
Plug the laptop into the radio DS port and try again if the kiosk cannot see the radio. Swap the cable.

steps.text: Does the kiosk still fail on this radio?

radio-ok.question: The radio looks healthy, so the problem is downstream at the DS or FMS. Does the DS show FMS Connected?

options.label: No, the DS does not show FMS Connected
Yes, FMS Connected but no robot communication

reboots.title: Radio reboots or drops in matches
steps: Dual power is usually fine and redundant. If the radio reboots, try removing one of PoE or the DC input, since dual power can occasionally cause odd issues.

steps.text: Is the radio powered from the switchable channel on the PDH?
steps.yes: Move it to a constant channel.

steps: Tug the Weidmuller plug. Re-strip and reseat the wires. Tie-wrap the cable to the frame near the radio.
Check the wire gauge and route. Thin wire on a long run drops voltage under load. Wire the radio to its own PDH or PDP channel.
Open the DS log. A battery dip below 7 V in a match resets the radio. Lower motor current limits and use a good battery.
Check nothing else is on the radio's channel. A shared channel with a motor browns out the radio.

steps.text: Does the radio still reboot or drop in matches?

ds-wifi.title: DS on Wi-Fi in the pit
steps: At an event the kiosk decides if the 2.4 GHz pit network is on. Many events turn it off. Use an Ethernet cable into the radio DS port instead.
The network name is the team number plus the kiosk suffix when 2.4 GHz is on. The password is the 2.4 GHz key.
DIP switch 3 forces standalone 2.4 GHz mode at home. Leave it off at events.
Turn the laptop Wi-Fi off before a match. On the field only Ethernet works.

steps.text: Is the network still missing?
steps.yes: Check whether 2.4 GHz pit Wi-Fi is on at this event.

radio-ds-fault.title: DS is not reaching FMS
steps: The DS is not connected to FMS. This is a DS problem, not the radio.
Use the Driver station guide in this app and work it fully before touching FMS.

radio-reset-net.title: FMS Connected but no robot comms
steps: Ping 10.TE.AM.2 from the DS to confirm the roboRIO is reachable through the radio.
Check the roboRIO Comm light. Off means the RIO is not talking to the DS.

steps.text: Is the RIO unreachable or the Comm light off?
steps.yes: Work the roboRIO side. Use the roboRIO guide.

steps: In FMS, open the prestart dropdown and choose Reset Networking.

steps.text: Did it recover?
steps.no: View the match logs and check whether other robots are affected too.

om5p.question: OpenMesh OM5P: what do the lights show?
om5p.help: The pre-2025 radio. Power, Eth Link and WiFi, left to right.

options.label: Power light is off
WiFi light is off or red on the field
It will not take a program

om5p-no-power.title: OM5P has no power
steps: The OM5P runs on 12 V. Wire it to a 12V 2A output on the VRM, centre pin positive.
Check the barrel plug is seated. Many barrel connectors look alike, so confirm it is the 12 V one.
If it is powered over PoE instead, check the injector and the Ethernet run.

steps.text: Is the Power light still off?

om5p-not-linked.title: OM5P is not linked to the field
steps: On the field the WiFi light should be green, which is bridge mode and linked.
Off means bridge mode with no link, or the radio is not running FRC firmware. Red means it is in access point mode, which is the at-home configuration.
Reprogram the radio with the FRC Radio Configuration Utility for this event.

steps.text: Is the WiFi light still not green on the field?

om5p-programming.title: OM5P will not take a program
steps: Plug the laptop straight into the radio port closest to the power jack. Nothing else connected by Ethernet.
Disable every other network adapter on the laptop, including Wi-Fi.
Run the FRC Radio Configuration Utility as administrator.
If it still will not find the radio, try the other port, or reach it on its programming address 192.168.1.1.

steps.text: Does it still refuse to program?
